rationale: PINS the SCOPE of the `exports` edge: Go scopes an identifier to its PACKAGE (spec, Declarations and blocks / Exported identifiers), and a capitalised name declared inside a function, method or func-literal body is unreachable from any importer. The lane deliberately publishes a function-local `type` as a SYMBOL — the declared-type pass attributes that type's field types to it, so dropping the symbol would publish a `references` edge whose source names nothing — and such a symbol carries no `ownerName`, so the symbol table cannot tell line 62 from line 28. Measured over a 500-file stride sample of go-stdlib (validation/m14/go/go-mislabel-probe.ts): 4,165 `exports` edges published, 11 of them for a name declared inside a function body, across test/fixedbugs/bug285.go (8) and src/cmd/compile/internal/test/align_test.go (3). Every one carried `exportForm: "capitalized_package_scope_name"`, so the edge was labelled with the rule it broke. EXPECTED rows are package-scope declarations; FORBIDDEN rows are the body-local declarations plus the lane's declared scope decision on methods and package-scope vars, which is pinned here so it stays a decision.
